scenes.headline: How a learnable activation mixes its own harmonics
scenes.sub: Learnable Spectral Activations, a small change inside coordinate networks
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Soffit! Here is how one small change to an activation helps a network draw sharp edges.

scenes.text: Earlier fixes choose which frequencies a network can use. This one learns how each neuron mixes them.
scenes.mark: learns how each neuron mixes them
scenes.say: A coordinate network turns a position into a value. Earlier fixes chose its frequencies. This one learns how each neuron mixes them.

left.title: Fixed activations
items: SIREN uses one sine per neuron
left.say: Fourier features, SIREN and FINER change the menu. Each neuron still emits one fixed waveform, welded to its feature.

right.title: Learned spectral activation
items: A few extra numbers per layer
right.say: Here the weights still pick the feature. A short list of learned numbers decides the waveform.

scenes.title: The activation
scenes.text: phi(u) = u + sum a_k sin(2 pi k u)

parts.note: a residual identity, where training starts
parts.say: It starts as the identity, so the network begins almost linear.

parts.note: integer harmonics of the same input
parts.say: Then it adds whole-number harmonics of the same input.

parts.note: learned, shared by every neuron in a layer
parts.say: Each harmonic gets a learned amplitude, shared by the whole layer.

steps.say: A coordinate goes through the weights, which choose what this neuron looks at.
The same value is fed to a bank of sines, one per harmonic.
Learned amplitudes weight and sum them, so one neuron can make a square edge on its own.
The output is linear in those amplitudes, so tuning the spectrum is a direct problem.
In the paper's toy test, SIREN and FINER need more atoms to fit a wiggly signal.
The learned harmonic unit fits it with one. The target suits it, so this shows the mechanism.

scenes.title: Kodak, mean PSNR
scenes.say: On twenty four Kodak photos the paper reports about thirty eight decibels, just ahead of FINER and three ahead of SIREN.

scenes.label: FINER's training step time, on full-grid audio
scenes.note: 64 extra parameters, but K sines per neuron
scenes.say: The parameters are almost free. The compute is not: a step takes nearly seven times as long as FINER's.

scenes.text: Tie a neuron's waveform to learned harmonic amplitudes, not to its weights, and edges get cheaper to learn.
scenes.say: The idea to keep: give each layer a learned recipe for mixing harmonics, and let the weights just pick features.
Frequencies picked. Harmonics mixed. Better fits, slower steps.
